forecast-period.text: A slow-moving high pressure system over the Tasman Sea extends a ridge over eastern SA. A trough of low pressure over western SA is moving eastwards and will reach southeastern parts later today while a weakening cold front crosses the Bight. The trough lingers in the east through the middle of the week as a weak high pressure system forms in the Bight. This trough weakens on Thursday as a second trough moves into the west from WA.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and possible thunderstorms in the west at first, extending to central and southeastern districts during the day. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to well above average through central parts. North to northeasterly winds, fresh at times, tending northwesterly ahead of a southerly change moving across the west during the day.

Showers and thunderstorms in the east and north. Maximum temperatures above average. North to northeasterly winds over eastern districts, tending northwesterly ahead of a southerly change moving throughout during the day.

Showers and possible thunderstorms in the north and east, clearing from the southeast during the evening. Maximum temperatures above average. South to southeasterly winds, turning east to northeasterly in the far west. Local afternoon seabreezes.

text.p: Areas of morning fog in the south. Showers and possible thunderstorms in the north. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to well above average near the coasts. North to northeasterly winds with local afternoon sea breezes. A southerly change moving into the west during the evening.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Thursday: 2 to 10 mm broadly across SA, increasing to 10 to 20 mm about the agricultural areas, Flinders Ranges and the far northwest. Isolated heavier falls of 20 to 40 mm are possible with thunderstorms extending from the Flinders Ranges south through the Mid North, Fleurieu Peninsula and into the east and southeast.
